raw_response:
**My reasoning:**

I have been farming this land for 40 years. I know what my family of 8 needs — we need wheat and maize above all else. Without those two, we do not eat. The wheat I plant in autumn after ploughing deep, and when it comes off in June I put maize in right away on the same ground. That is what my mother did and what everyone here does. Those 5 mu of wheat-maize ground are the backbone.

Cotton I have grown since I was young. I know how to read it, when to water it, when the bollworm is coming. The price has gone up and down but I know this crop with my eyes closed. I will keep 3 mu on it.

Stevia is what the buyers come for now. It has been good to me these past years. I keep 2 mu. It needs more water than the other crops but the well is there. I cut it several times across summer and autumn.

The little millet patch — less than 1 mu — I grow for ourselves. Old variety, same seeds I have used for years. It barely needs watering and it keeps well through winter.

I will plough the wheat and cotton ground the old way, deep. For maize I use the rotary — it is faster after the wheat comes off and I am not as strong as I was. I apply fertilizer in two doses the way I always have: base fertilizer before planting, top-dressing when the plant is growing. I use the compound bags from the village shop. I do not measure exactly — I go by what looks right and what has worked.
